titleStmt.title: declaration by the munshi of the legation.

head.hi: declaration by the munshi of the legation.

div.p:
I, Mirza Abul Kassan Khan, the chief munshi of the United States legation, in compliance with the orders of his excellency the minister of the United States, on the evening of Friday the 23 of Jamadi the second, A. H., corresponding to the 13th of January, 1893, went to the chief police office of this city for the purpose of being a witness to the punishment of Ali Akbar Khan, who hall insulted Mrs. Esselstyn, a native of the United States of America, in the public streets, hereby testify that eighteen stripes with a cat of five tails (over a thin coat and shirt) were given on the back and shoulders of Ali Akbar Khan, and so severely was the punishment
inflicted that the culprit was overcome by it, and he cried and begged for mercy. Thereupon I, on the part of the legation and the lady insulted, ordered the boy to be released and be let go.
Then, in my presence, a bond was taken from the culprit, his brother, and uncle, binding him over to keep the peace toward Mrs. Esselstyn for the remainder of his wife.
